text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam has decided to provide 10,000 tonnes of rice to the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.
-- The spread of the deadly disease AIDS is continuing across Vietnam with an estimated 300,000 cases expected by the turn of the century, the National AIDS Committee announced.
-- About 200 billion dong ($17 million) of the state budget was spent in organizing the National Assembly election on July 20.

-- Industries where investment is prohibited in Vietnam's industrial and hi-tech parks include atomic power, production of radio-active substances, industrial explosives, harmful chemicals, leather-tanning and dyeing substances.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi has said the industrialisation and modernisation of the country could not be successful without an oil industry.

-- National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh has highlighted the success of the recent National Assembly election saying it had ensured democracy and conformity with legislation while proceeding as scheduled, safely and economically.
-- A country-wide conference to review the result of voting for the National Assembly's 10th session was held in Ho Chi Minh City on Monday.

-- Representatives of the National Assembly and People's Councils need to do more to bring into play the people's mastership and to meet their roles in monitoring the state, the acting chairman of the Ho Chi Minh City People's Council has said.
